speaker: Mr Low Thia Khiang
text: asked	the Minister for Education (Schools) whether the Ministry reviews the criteria used by individual primary schools to determine whether students are allowed to take up Higher Mother Tongue to ensure that reasonable consideration is given to students' interest in the subject instead of it being a purely results-driven process.

speaker: The Parliamentary Secretary to the Ministers for Education (Ms Low Yen Ling) (for the Minister for Education (Schools))
text: This is a positive sign for a strong bilingual foundation.

speaker: The Parliamentary Secretary to the Ministers for Education (Ms Low Yen Ling) (for the Minister for Education (Schools))
text: This is because Higher Mother Tongue means additional curriculum time and heavier learning load.

speaker: The Parliamentary Secretary to the Ministers for Education (Ms Low Yen Ling) (for the Minister for Education (Schools))
text: The subject can be overwhelming to students who are not interested or not ready to take up the subject.

speaker: The Parliamentary Secretary to the Ministers for Education (Ms Low Yen Ling) (for the Minister for Education (Schools))
text: In addition, schools are also guided by the learning profiles of the students and the schools are very mindful of the interest and the overall well-being of the child.

speaker: The Parliamentary Secretary to the Ministers for Education (Ms Low Yen Ling) (for the Minister for Education (Schools))
text: In addition, the Ministry of Education (MOE) regularly reminds our schools of the considerations that should guide their offer of various subjects to their students.

speaker: The Parliamentary Secretary to the Ministers for Education (Ms Low Yen Ling) (for the Minister for Education (Schools))
text: We also provide close guidance and work closely with schools that need additional support in this area.

speaker: Mr Low Thia Khiang (Aljunied)
text: How much weightage is given to a student's interest and family support, for example, and the other consideration of the results of the various subjects?

speaker: Mr Low Thia Khiang (Aljunied)
text: Do they encourage students to do so and, if so, are there schemes to guide schools to encourage students who are qualified to take up Higher Chinese?

speaker: Ms Low Yen Ling
text: I want to thank the Member for the supplementary questions.

speaker: Ms Low Yen Ling
text: First off, let me give some context to Higher Chinese language (HCL).

speaker: Ms Low Yen Ling
text: They admit students who are inclined towards learning Chinese at a higher level.

speaker: Ms Low Yen Ling
text: Since the HCL curriculum is available, some other non-SAP primary schools have also offered it to students with stronger aptitude and interest in the language.

speaker: Ms Low Yen Ling
text: We all know learning language is not just for conversing or writing.

speaker: Ms Low Yen Ling
text: So, it is important that the student has a strong affinity and interest in that subject, so that we can nurture the joy of learning in the children and sustain their interest in the HCL even after they leave school.

speaker: Ms Low Yen Ling
text: To this end, we are heartened by the enthusiasm that parents and students have shown for the HCL.

speaker: Ms Low Yen Ling
text: We want to assure the Member and the House that our schools are deeply committed to the teaching and learning of Higher Mother Tongue languages.

speaker: Ms Low Yen Ling
text: We do so because it is not just mastering a higher level of Chinese, but also deepening bilingualism, which is an integral part of our national identity and cultural heritage.

speaker: Ms Low Yen Ling
text: Another point that I would like to reassure the Member and the House is that our schools strive to cater to students of different learning capabilities and also home languages, depending on whether they speak English or Mandarin at home.

speaker: Ms Low Yen Ling
text: Students are able to take their Mother Tongue at the level which best suits their ability.

speaker: Ms Low Yen Ling
text: The Member may ask why is that important.

speaker: Ms Low Yen Ling
text: This differentiated approach is very important because it allows the school to customise the level of support for the child's learning.

speaker: Ms Low Yen Ling
text: When the learning is pitched at their level and ability, the students can learn the Mother Tongue language to as high a level as they can, and are also given adequate opportunities and support.

speaker: Ms Low Yen Ling
text: This is important so that we can help to nurture the children's learning of the Mother Tongue and sustain their interest in this language, even beyond school.

speaker: Mr Low Thia Khiang
text: There were complaints by parents that even when students got over 90 marks for Chinese language and when they are interested and motivated to learn the language, they are not admitted to the Higher Chinese class.

speaker: Ms Low Yen Ling
text: I want to thank Mr Low for the supplementary question.

speaker: Ms Low Yen Ling
text: We acknowledge St Hilda's Primary School's good intentions in making sure that the students who want to take HCL are well-suited and 	are also ready to take on the subject because it also entails extra curriculum time and a heavier study load for the child.

speaker: Mdm Speaker
